title: Disability Benefit Terms — Payment Protection
content:
Disability of a covered person is a protected event on four Payment Protection plans. On the other two, Payment Protection Life and Joint Payment Protection Life, every disability term reads "not covered".

## Disability terms by plan

| Plan | Elimination period (continuous days of disability before benefits begin) | Benefits paid from | Most monthly benefits per claim | Most monthly benefits over the plan's life | Pre-existing condition look-back (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Protection Life | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Payment Protection Life and Disability | 30 | retroactive to the first day of disability | 12 | 24 | 180 |
| Payment Protection Complete | 30 | retroactive to the first day of disability | 12 | 24 | 180 |
| Joint Payment Protection Life | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered | not covered |
| Joint Payment Protection Life and Disability | 30 | retroactive to the first day of disability | 12 | 24 | 180 |
| Joint Payment Protection Complete | 30 | retroactive to the first day of disability | 12 | 24 | 180 |

## Points of judgement

- **Elimination period.** Benefits begin only once the covered person has been continuously disabled for the elimination period (30 days on the four disability plans). Once that is met, benefits are paid back to the first day of disability.
- **Pre-existing conditions.** A condition treated within the look-back period before enrollment is excluded for the same number of days after enrollment. With the 180-day look-back, a condition treated within 180 days before enrollment is excluded for 180 days after enrollment.
- **Month limits.** One disability claim receives at most 12 monthly benefits, and the plan as a whole receives at most 24 monthly disability benefits over its life.
